heading: Montana Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Montana paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Montana income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and provide your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Montana introduced significant income tax and payroll withholding changes in 2026. Using outdated withholding allowances or older state tax rates could result in an inaccurate paycheck estimate.

Whether you work in Billings, Missoula, Bozeman, Great Falls or another Montana community, this calculator can help you compare employment opportunities and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the Montana Paycheck Calculator

Begin by choosing annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross earnings before taxes and select your payment frequency.

Enter the federal and Montana income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub, including additional or fixed withholding already reflected in those amounts.

Add retirement contributions, healthcare premiums and other employee deductions.

Review the results to understand your estimated gross pay, individual taxes and remaining take-home income.

Use your most recent pay stub and current withholding certificate to obtain a more representative estimate.

## Montana Payroll Taxes in 2026

Montana employees generally encounter the following payroll deductions.

Your actual deductions depend on earnings, filing status, withholding elections and employee benefits.

The [Montana Department of Revenue](https://revenue.mt.gov/) provides official state income tax and employer withholding information.

## What Changed in Montana Income Tax in 2026?

Montana updated its income tax brackets and reduced its top marginal rate beginning January 1, 2026.

The previous top rate of 5.9% decreased to 5.65%.

The lower 4.7% rate also applies to a broader range of taxable income.

The applicable threshold depends on the taxpayer's filing classification.

The 5.65% rate applies to qualifying taxable income exceeding the applicable threshold.

These thresholds relate to taxable income after applicable deductions, rather than gross salary.

Read the official [Montana 2026 withholding update](https://revenue.mt.gov/news/recent-news/2026-withholding-updates) for an explanation of the changes.

## Montana's New Withholding Method

Montana changed more than its income tax rates in 2026.

The ordinary payroll withholding calculation no longer relies on the previous Montana personal allowance system, including separate state personal and dependent exemptions.

Instead, the updated methodology relies on the applicable federal filing classification and federal standard deduction amount.

Employees can still request additional withholding or elect an applicable fixed withholding amount.

This distinction matters because a calculator that continues using the old allowance-based methodology may produce incorrect results even if it uses the updated tax rates.

The [Montana Employer and Information Agent Guide](https://www.revenue.mt.gov/publications/montana-employer-and-information-agent-guide) provides the official employer tables and calculation procedures.

## Understanding Montana Form MW-4

Montana employees generally complete Form MW-4 to provide state withholding information to their employers.

The updated 2026 certificate accounts for filing status, multiple jobs, additional withholding and qualifying exemption arrangements.

Employees with multiple jobs or married employees whose spouses also work should review the applicable worksheet when determining additional withholding.

Montana does not accept the federal Form W-4 as a replacement for its current state withholding certificate.

You can obtain the updated [Montana Employee's Withholding and Exemption Certificate](https://revenue.mt.gov/publications/montana-employees-withholding-allowance-and-exemption-certificate-form-mw-4) from the Department of Revenue.

Review your selections when starting a new job or experiencing a substantial change in household income.

## Montana Income Tax Calculation Example

To understand the marginal tax structure, consider a single taxpayer with $50,000 in taxable income after applicable deductions.

The first $47,500 is subject to the lower 4.7% rate.

$47,500 × 4.7% = $2,232.50

The remaining taxable income is:

$50,000 − $47,500 = $2,500

Tax on the remaining portion:

$2,500 × 5.65% = $141.25

Total illustrated income tax:

$2,232.50 + $141.25 = $2,373.75

The example explains the marginal tax rates rather than establishing a complete paycheck withholding calculation.

Your employer must apply the official payroll methodology, including applicable withholding adjustments and rounding.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Montana Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal income tax withholding depends on taxable earnings, filing status, payroll frequency and Form W-4 information.

Multiple jobs, other income, eligible credits and additional withholding requests may change the amount deducted.

Review [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) for the official calculation procedures.

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security.

The 2026 annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500.

An employee receiving $2,500 in covered earnings before reaching the annual limit would contribute $155.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings.

There is no standard annual taxable wage ceiling for ordinary Medicare.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% on Medicare-covered wages exceeding $200,000 paid by that employer during the calendar year.

The [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) explains these federal payroll contributions.

## Montana Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider a Montana employee earning $65,000 annually before taxes and deductions.

Assume all earnings are covered by ordinary Social Security and Medicare contributions.

For federal withholding, assume the employee is single, uses a modern Form W-4 and has no additional adjustments.

Approximately $2,092.60 remains before Montana income tax and other employee deductions.

Enter your Montana withholding amount to obtain a more complete net paycheck estimate.

## Montana Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate gross earnings using their hourly rate and working hours.

Suppose you earn $28 per hour and work 40 regular hours plus five qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$28 × 40 = $1,120

Overtime earnings:

$28 × 1.5 × 5 = $210

Total gross earnings:

$1,330

Assuming ordinary federal payroll contribution coverage, Social Security would be $82.46 and Medicare would be approximately $19.29.

Federal and Montana income tax withholding would also apply.

Employees working in construction, tourism, agriculture and other seasonal industries may experience variable working hours and earnings.

Review the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for applicable eligibility requirements.

## Does Montana Have Local Employee Income Taxes?

Montana municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes.

Employees are still subject to applicable federal and Montana income taxes and payroll contributions.

Montana also does not impose a general statewide sales tax, although certain communities may impose authorized local resort taxes.

These taxes and household expenses should be considered separately from employment paycheck deductions.

## Working in Montana and Living in Another State

Employees near Montana's borders may work in one state while residing in another.

Montana and North Dakota have a reciprocal income tax arrangement for qualifying employee compensation.

Employees may need to provide the applicable withholding certificate before receiving reciprocal treatment.

Living in a state without wage income tax does not automatically eliminate Montana tax on Montana-sourced employment earnings.

Remote work and interstate employment may require additional income allocation calculations.

Consult the Montana Department of Revenue before claiming exemption from state withholding.

## Managing Seasonal Earnings in Montana

Montana's tourism, agriculture and outdoor recreation industries can create seasonal employment patterns.

If your working hours fluctuate significantly, avoid using your highest-earning paycheck as the basis for your entire [annual budget](/calculators/budget-calculator/).

Estimate earnings during both busy and quieter periods.

Compare take-home income alongside housing, transportation, insurance and essential household expenses.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a financial cushion for periods of reduced employment.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Montana's income tax rate in 2026?

Montana uses rates of 4.7% and 5.65% under its 2026 tax structure. Applicable filing thresholds and withholding adjustments determine the amount deducted from your paycheck.

### Did Montana change its payroll withholding rules in 2026?

Yes. Montana updated its rates, thresholds and withholding methodology beginning January 1, 2026. The ordinary calculation no longer uses the previous state personal allowance system.

### Does Montana have municipal employee income taxes?

Montana municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes on ordinary employment earnings.
